_comment: CalculiX family extensions: ccx-modal (natural frequencies) and ccx-thermal (steady-state conduction). Self-contained adapters in simlab/solvers/ that reuse the aces golden conforming mesher (gmsh 4.15.2 C3D10) and ccx 2.23 inside the aces-golden:0.1 image. A drop-in so simlab/solvers.json is never rewritten. Validated on the rig 2026-10-12 through the queue in --docker mode; the numbers below are the queue's own results.json, copied to docs/validation/ccx-20261012/.

ccx-modal.description: Natural frequencies of a watertight part.stl: gmsh 4.15.2 C3D10 (tet10, second-order linear, single-thread mesher) via the aces golden conforming mesher, ccx 2.23 *FREQUENCY (SPOOLES) on the rig CPU; mm-N-s-tonne consistent units, eigenfrequencies parsed from ccx.dat. Refuses to run without material.rho_kg_mm3 (no mass matrix, no meaningful modes).

validation.device: rig cpu x8 (ccx 2.23 at /usr/local/bin/ccx, sha256 31be21fc2f0902bd9a05acc2651dbac6dc2a2573dabbf235e39a38cb6f458862; gmsh 4.15.2)

cases.case: 100 x 10 x 10 mm steel cantilever (cases/ccx_validation/beam_100x10x10.stl), root face x=0 clamped (153 surface nodes), 2 mm C3D10 (6989 elements, 12129 nodes, remesh route, volume exactly 10000 mm3, min SICN 0.191), *FREQUENCY 6 modes, SPOOLES
cases.note: reference is Euler-Bernoulli (beta_n^2/2 pi) sqrt(EI/(rho A L^4)); modes 1/2 are the two equal bending planes of the square section (812.834 / 812.841 Hz). EB neglects shear deformation, so the 3-D solid solve sits below it, more so for the shorter wavelength of mode 3 (-4.6 %). eigenfrequencies_hz: [812.834, 812.8409, 4874.668, 4874.711, 7204.903, 12655.46].

validation.note: Ran through the rig queue in --docker mode (experiment ccx-modal-cantilever-v1, case c000, job ccx-modal-cantilever-v1--c000--run--761496); ccx rc 0, no *ERROR/*WARNING.

ccx-thermal.description: Steady-state heat conduction in a watertight part.stl: gmsh 4.15.2 C3D10 via the aces golden conforming mesher, ccx 2.23 *HEAT TRANSFER STEADY STATE on the rig CPU; named surface boundaries carry fixed temperatures (*BOUNDARY dof 11) or heat flux into the body (*DFLUX); nodal temperatures parsed from ccx.dat. Refuses to run without material.conductivity, and without at least one temperature boundary (pure-flux steady state is singular).

validation.device: rig cpu x8 (ccx 2.23 at /usr/local/bin/ccx, sha256 31be21fc2f0902bd9a05acc2651dbac6dc2a2573dabbf235e39a38cb6f458862; gmsh 4.15.2)

cases.case: 50 x 10 x 10 mm slab (cases/ccx_validation/slab_50x10x10.stl), k = 0.05 W/(mm K) = 50 W/(m K), 20 degC fixed at x=0, 0.1 W/mm2 *DFLUX into the body at x=50 (66 faces, 100 mm2), sides insulated; 2 mm C3D10 (3571 elements, 6262 nodes, volume exactly 5000 mm3)
cases.note: closed form delta T = q L / k = 0.1 * 50 / 0.05 = 100 K; a linear temperature field is exact on tetrahedra, so the 0.0 rel_err is the expected outcome, and it confirms the DFLUX face mapping (ccx S-labels) and conductivity units end to end. ccx printed the benign warning '*WARNING reading *HEAT TRANSFER: a nonlinear geometric analysis is requested' (default NLGEOM); recorded here rather than hidden.

validation.note: Ran through the rig queue in --docker mode (experiment ccx-thermal-slab-v1, case c000, job ccx-thermal-slab-v1--c000--run--ae83ec); ccx rc 0.
